title: macos's commit-stamp check refuses a sha256 repository's 64-character stamp
body:
Found by the critic-shell pass on ST0011/06a's re-bank (dc, 2026-10-31), predating WP06 (issue 0243): lib/cmd/macos checks the commit stamp a build carries against the pattern {8,40}, so a sha256 repository's 64-character stamp is refused as no stamp, while the stage's commit record check beside it (WP06a, is_commit_sha full) accepts 64. Two readers of one fact disagree about the repository's object format. Fix: a stamp form of is_commit_sha in lib/helpers (an abbreviation of eight or more characters, or a whole name of 40 or 64), used by the stamp check; one arm in helpers.bats red at the base. Lands with issue 0298's helpers unit, which gives git_head_sha the same discipline on an unknown form.

## Resolution

Fixed at 99005dbc30370ba04a061b570f912948e759e61f, landed on main by devbin-vc's land-stack.sh as one unit of group B's four (0298, 0299, 0311, 0305), unpushed until the 0.1.20 cut. is_commit_sha gains a stamp form, an abbreviation of eight or more lowercase hex characters up to a whole name of either object format, and macos's commit-stamp check reads through it, so a sha256 repository's 64-character stamp is a stamp, as its record is a record. docs/configuration.md says the same. helpers.bats holds the form to real sha1 and sha256 names, and macos.bats's refusal arm reads the new wording. It was proved in group B's run on pplr-vc's desk, with each driver's kit read by devbin-vc first. In slot 01M6KY03231VVJCH6JMSK3J20X at df972df8, every unit's arms were red in its own red clone (its parent with its tests on top) and green at the tip under BSD and GNU, with every file that reaches the changed code, help and the tree scans. One arm, 0311's, trapped INT, which a backgrounded GNU leg starts with ignored. Once that arm was fixed, the targeted rerun in slot 01M6KZPRCRBPAY42KCVWWSKHF9 at b4e2a066 exited rc 0. critic-shell reviewed the stack once and every finding was settled.
